area: Enemy AI: attack tokens, cadence, telegraphs

items.title: Attack token / combat-director pattern (DOOM token pool, slot systems)
items.claim: The shipped-game pattern for 'enemies take turns' is an explicit token pool: each attack type has N tokens, an enemy must acquire one before attacking and returns it after; pool size directly caps simultaneous attackers (DOOM 2016, per Kurt Loudy/Jake Campbell GDC material), with token-stealing so the nearest/most-threatening enemy stays active. Practitioner interviews (Vossen, covering DmC/GoW3/Arkham-class melee) confirm the same 'slot system' regulating who strikes when, plus near/far grouping where only the near group may attack. Nobody ships turn-taking as an emergent side effect of independent timers; it is always an explicit, testable cap.

sources.title: Cyber Demons: The AI of DOOM (2016) — Tommy Thompson, Game Developer
GDC Vault — Bringing Hell to Life: AI and Full Body Animation in DOOM (Jake Campbell, id Software)
Enemy design and enemy AI for melee combat systems — Bart Vossen (designer interviews), Game Developer

items.adjudication_reason: Ledger gap-H row 'simultaneous attackers' measures TURNS (1, occasionally 2; 8-on-screen hit rate no higher than 1v1) and itself says 'Implement an attack token' — but src/core/AISeamController.ts's header contract asserts 'NO ATTACK TOKEN... EMERGENT from independent AI_THINK_INTERVAL_MS timers plus the narrow AI_MELEE_RANGE gate'. That emergence claim has never been chaos-tested against the measured invariant, and with ENCOUNTER_SIZE=8 mobs (src/config/mobs.ts) all converging into the same 50-px AI_MELEE_RANGE band, each rolling aggression every 500 ms independently, >2 simultaneous attackers is the expected outcome, not turn-taking.
items.implementation_note: Gate first, mechanism second (repo chaos-test rule): add a deterministic 8-mob harness metric asserting (a) max simultaneous telegraph/attack-mode enemies <= 2 and (b) player hits-taken rate ~ 1v1 baseline. If the emergent mechanism fails, add a minimal Sim-owned (or EncounterDirector in core/) SINGLE token — grant to nearest in-range enemy, occasional second grant (rare, per gap-H 'occasionally 2'), release on recover-start. Do NOT copy DOOM's per-attack-type pools or difficulty-scaled pool sizes — kunai is already range+chance gated in AISeamController, and the OG's measured cap is 1(-2), not a tunable. Token lives in core/, zero literals, values in src/config/ai.ts tagged CONTRACT (gap-H).

items.title: Two-case telegraph (600 ms approach / 267 ms point-blank), no telegraph VFX
items.claim: Telegraph literature says anticipation must exceed player reaction (~0.25 s) plus ability-trigger time plus a difficulty buffer, and telegraph length should vary per attack context rather than being one global number (GDKeys 'Anatomy of an Attack'; Hornet case study uses 15-40+ frame telegraphs per move). The OG's measured pair — 0.600 s while closing, 0.267 s point-blank repeat — is exactly a per-context telegraph where the repeat sits at the raw reaction floor.

items.adjudication_reason: src/config/ai.ts AI_TELEGRAPH_MS = { closing: 600, pointBlank: 267 } (CONTRACT-SRC), selected by range at commit time in AISeamController.next() via AI_POINT_BLANK_X; the old single-global >=520 ms telegraph was deleted SESSION13 D8. Ledger gap-H rows 'telegraph, approach attack' and 'telegraph, point-blank repeat' are the source.
items.implementation_note: Two guard rails: (1) gap-H 'telegraph FX: none — pose change only. Do NOT give enemies a drawn stroke line' — the generic best practice of adding warning icons/flash VFX (Arkham-style lightning) would be a fidelity DEFECT here; keep OpponentIntent.telegraph as a pose/windup cue only in the scene. (2) AI_POINT_BLANK_X = 25 is honestly labeled INFERRED — the case boundary is the one unmeasured number; a future video pass could bracket where 600 ms flips to 267 ms.
items.stage: now (nothing to build; protect in review)

items.title: Blocking the OG doesn't have — the flagged AISeamController blocking is already deleted
items.claim: Defensive reactions (block/parry/dodge) are a per-game design choice, not a melee-AI requirement — Vossen's interviews treat them as optional context reactions. The OG measured ZERO blocks/parries/dodges in ~70 s across ~30 enemies (gap-H clean negative), so modeling any is inventing behavior.

items.title: Gait split + speed retune: trash walks ~128 stage px/s, bosses ONLY run — single ENEMY_SPEED is wrong on both counts
items.claim: Shipped melee AI differentiates approach behavior per archetype (Vossen: near/far groups, per-enemy approach roles) and full-body animation gait sells the enemy's intent (DOOM GDC animation talk). The OG measured: trash approach gait is WALK ONLY, median 128 stage px/s (105-161 band, gap-H — the earlier 22 px/tick reading was a peak and builds mobs ~25% too fast); duel bosses NEVER walk — all approach/retreat legs are deep-lean runs at 573-716 px/s @1080 = 255-318 world px/s (§S24-D boss correction); both classes dash only as the attack opener.

items.implementation_note: Split ENEMY_SPEED into MOB_WALK_SPEED ~= 106.7 world px/s (128 stage /1.2, CONTRACT per gap-H) and BOSS_RUN_SPEED in 255-318 world px/s (CONTRACT per §S24-D; note the player's MOVE_RUN_PX_S 288 already sits in-band — reusing it keys the gait picker on speed alone, as §S24-D recommends). Route the class through the AITierParams table or a mob/boss flag on the controller. Update the double-entry in tests/config-values.test.ts in the same commit (config CLAUDE.md ratchet).

items.title: Enemy attack = dash-THROUGH (commit ~194 stage px, resolve ~96 px PAST), not a stationary strike inside a 50-px gate
items.claim: DOOM's GDC material frames enemy attacks as full-body animation commitments the AI cannot take back — the attack IS a movement, and readability comes from that committed travel. The OG measured exactly this shape: the enemy attack is a dash-THROUGH using the same mechanic as the player — commit at ~194 stage px, lunge at ~484 stage px/s (~3.3x walk), damage resolving at the END of the dash when the enemy is ~96 stage px PAST the player; the gap-H row states outright 'a radius check cannot reproduce this'.

items.adjudication_reason: Current pipeline is exactly the radius check gap-H forbids: AISeamController only telegraphs inside AI_MELEE_RANGE (|dx|<50 && dy<50 world, CONTRACT-SRC per D8) and the Sim's enemy-strike handler (src/core/Sim.ts, 'Enemy strike: telegraph timing/range are the CONTROLLER's job') resolves in place with no enemy travel — no commit-at-range, no pass-through, no resolve-past-target. Ledger rows: gap-H 'attack geometry' + §S24-E (line-follow + terminal snap model, flagged as A12.2 input).
items.implementation_note: Reconcile the apparent conflict instead of overwriting the CONTRACT-SRC gate: model TWO attack entries mirroring the two telegraphs — (1) approach-attack: commit at ~161.7 world px (194 stage /1.2), 600 ms telegraph, then a lunge (484 stage = ~403 world px/s) THROUGH the player, damage on the terminal tick ~80 world px (96 stage) past; (2) point-blank repeat: inside the 50-px source gate, 267 ms telegraph, same pass-through resolution. Reuse the Sim's existing dash/line-follow machinery (§S24-E stepper) rather than a new mover. This also naturally explains why AI_POINT_BLANK_X exists. Chaos test: a jumping player must evade the terminal tick, not the whole travel (gap-K tension: approach-run deals zero damage, only the dash phase damages).

items.title: Per-enemy attack cadence: validate against the measured 0.467-1.933 s landed-hit band, not the genre's 2-3 s default
items.claim: Practitioner guidance says melee enemies typically attack every 2-3 s to keep crowds readable (Vossen's designer interviews) — but the OG is measurably FASTER: landed-hit cadence min 0.467 s, median 0.733 s, mean 0.853 s, max 1.933 s (n=10, gap-H). Adopting the genre default would slow the game ~3x; the cadence must be derived from the measurement and pinned by a harness.

items.adjudication_reason: src/config/ai.ts AITierParams attackMs/recoverMs (180/760, 180/620, 160/480) plus AI_THINK_INTERVAL_MS 500 and AI_RECOVER_JITTER_FRAC 0.35 are spec-era values never reconciled against ledger gap-H's 'cadence (landed hits)' row; the composed inter-hit distribution of the current state machine (telegraph 600/267 + attack ~180 + recover 480-760 jittered + 500 ms decision beats + aggression roll) has no test asserting it lands in 0.467-1.933 s with median ~0.733 s.
items.implementation_note: Add a seeded harness (same pattern as DUEL_TARGET_SECONDS' 24-seed band in tests/harness.test.ts) that runs a stationary-player duel and asserts landed-hit inter-arrival min/median/max inside the gap-H band; then retune recoverMs per tier until green and relabel those values CONTRACT-derived. Do this AFTER the dash-through rework (previous item) — cadence composes with attack travel time, so tuning first would be tuned twice.

dead_ends: No primary Rocksteady source for Arkham's attacker concurrency was found — searches surfaced only community guides (Steam/Fandom/GameFAQs) and Costiuc's third-party analysis; the specific claim 'Arkham enemies attack one at a time by design' could not be grounded to a developer statement, so it is not used as a load-bearing claim. God of War 2018/Ragnarok attack-token specifics: the GDC Vault talk 'Preparing AI Systems for God of War Ragnarok' exists but its indexed summary covers behavior-tree migration/awareness/vertical movement, not tokens — not cited for token claims. DOOM's exact token-grant timing/cadence numbers (from the 2018 'Embracing Push Forward Combat' talk) were not retrievable in text form — only the mechanism, not its millisecond parameters, is grounded; the repo's cadence numbers come from the ledger instead, which is the correct precedence here anyway.
